'''Glenn Alan Robinson III''' (born January 8, 1994) is an American basketball player who played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] for two years ending with the [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2013–14 team]]. He was an All-State high school basketball player for [[Lake Central High School]] in Indiana. He is the son of [[Glenn Robinson]], the 1994 [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|NBA first overall draft pick]].

In high school, he committed to the [[University of Michigan]] before his junior season while he was still a three-star prospect ranked outside of the top 100 in the national class of 2012, according to [[Rivals.com]]. By the end of his high school career, he was a five-star top 20 prospect in the national class, according to some, including Rivals and [[ESPN.com]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/103517/glenn-robinson|title=Glenn Robinson|accessdate=Feb 2, 2013|date=April 6, 2012|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> Nonetheless, he was overlooked by many prestigious honors selectors, but he did appear in some national All-American contests. Subsequently, he began his college career at Michigan where he was an immediate starter for the [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2012–13 team]]. Following the [[2012–13 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2012–13 Big Ten season]] he was recognized as an honorable mention All-conference selection and All-freshman honoree by the coaches. He was selected to the Kyle Macy Freshman All-American Team. He was again recognized as an honorable mention All-conference selection following the [[2013–14 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2013–14 Big Ten season]].

==Background==
Robinson was born, weighing {{convert|3|lbs|4|oz|kg}}, three months premature to his single [[Purdue University]] freshman mother, Shantelle Clay, at Methodist Hospital in [[Gary, Indiana]].<ref name=GRIgis/> He spent his first two months in an [[incubator (neonatal)|incubator]] (with a miniature [[basketball (ball)|basketball]]), until he was about {{convert|6|lbs|kg}}.<ref name=GRIgis>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/colleges/michigan/basketball/story/_/id/7159849/glenn-robinson-eager-join-michigan-wolverines|title=Glenn Robinson III grows into star: Born prematurely and clinging to life, son of 'Big Dog' has blossomed into U-M commit|accessdate=2012-11-14|date=2011-10-28|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Rothstein, Michael}}</ref> By age three he was a participant in the [[Hammond, Indiana]] [[YMCA]] children's basketball league.<ref name=GRIgis/> Robinson attended Grimmer Middle School prior to attending [[Lake Central High School]].<ref name=Bbpoty/>  He stood at {{convert|5|ft|6|in|m}} in seventh grade and {{convert|6|ft|1|in|m}} two years later as a freshman.<ref name=GRIgis/> Robinson was nearly {{convert|6|ft|4|in|m}} during his sophomore season and stood at over {{convert|6|ft|5.5|in|m|2}} as a junior.<ref name=GRIbtfsoaNptctMb/>

As a freshman, he played [[junior varsity]] for Lake Central and once made a game-winning half-court shot.<ref name=LWiC/> That year he became obsessed with his dream of dunking and even bought special shoes and wore [[ankle weight]]s to help his dream come true.<ref name=LWiC/> At the time, his father lived in Atlanta and Robinson grew up with his mother, Shantelle Clay-Irving and younger brother Gelen.<ref name=LWiC/> During the summer between his freshman and sophomore season, he came under the wing of two substitute father figures: Dave Milausnic, Lake Central Varsity Basketball head coach, and Wayne Brumm, AAU SYF Players under-17 coach.<ref name=LWiC/> Milausnic convinced Robinson to come to the gym for early morning workouts, often waking Robinson at his home.<ref name=LWiC/> Brumm, who would eventually continue to mentor Robinson as a collegian, advised Robinson to hire a personal trainer named Andrew Wallen, who helped Robinson augment his [[vertical leap]]. He also helped Robinson bulk up from {{convert|167|lbs|kg|2}} prior to his sophomore year to {{convert|210|lbs|kg|2}} in two years.<ref name=LWiC/> Growing up, Robinson has not embodied the tough vocal demeanor that his father had and the his brother developed. His passive nature has shown itself in all facets of Robinson's life including his basketball game.<ref name=LWiC/>

===2013 NBA Draft===
On April 9 before boarding the airplane to return from the NCAA Final Four, Beilein met with [[Trey Burke]], Hardaway, Robinson and [[Mitch McGary|McGary]] to direct them to seek the advice of the NBA advisory committee. The draft board had until April 15 to develop each individual report and the players had until April 28 to enter the draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2013/04/michigan_nba_prospects_seeking.html|title=Michigan's NBA prospects seeking advice from draft board, John Beilein being 'proactive' with process|accessdate=2013-04-11|date=2013-04-11|work=MLive.com|author=Baumgardner, Nick}}</ref> On April 12, ESPN journalist Myron Medcalf described Robinson's likelihood of entering the draft as "borderline," noting it was a tough choice between becoming a professional player and being the Big Man on Campus.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9163283/a-look-college-underclassmen-decided-undecided-nba-draft-college-basketball|title=Underclassmen: To go or not to go?|accessdate=2013-04-12|date=2013-04-12|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Medcalf, Myron}}</ref> Several sources regarded him as a likely first round draft choice in the NBA Draft,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/04/18/nba-michigan-mitch-mcgary-glenn-robinson-iii/2094233/|title=Michigan's McGary, Robinson III to return, wait on NBA|accessdate=2013-04-18|date=2013-04-18|work=[[USA Today]]|author=Snyder, Mark}}</ref><ref name=MRwrf2s>{{cite web|url=http://www.michigandaily.com/sports/mcgary-robinson-will-return-2013-14-season|title=McGary, Robinson will return for 2013-14 season|accessdate=2013-04-18|date=2013-04-18|work=[[Michigan Daily]]|author=Thomas, Colleen}}</ref> so there was much speculation about him entering his name into the draft. On April 18, he and McGary held a joint press conference to announce that they would not enter the draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/22097882/mcgary-robinson-iii-returning-to-michigan-instead-of-leaving-for-nba|title=McGary, Robinson III returning to Michigan instead of leaving for NBA|accessdate=2013-04-18|date=2013-04-18|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> This came after Burke and Hardaway entered the draft on the 14th<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/04/14/michigan-trey-burke-declares-for-nba-draft/2081881/|title=Michigan's Trey Burke declares for NBA draft|accessdate=2013-04-14|date=2013-04-14|work=[[USA Today]]|author=Snyder, Mark}}</ref><ref name=TBeNd>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/id/9170466/trey-burke-michigan-wolverines-announces-entering-nba-draft|title=Trey Burke enters NBA draft|accessdate=2013-04-14|date=2013-04-14|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Rothstein, Michael}}</ref> and 17th,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/id/9183145/nba-draft-2013-tim-hardaway-jr-michigan-wolverines-enter-nba-draft |title=Tim Hardaway Jr. to enter draft |accessdate=2013-04-19|accessdate=2013-04-17|date=2013-04-17|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Rothstein, Michael}}</ref> respectively. He is the son of Shantelle Clay (also known as Shantelle Clay-Irving)<ref name=LWiC/> and [[Glenn Robinson]], who was [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]],<ref name=LRctphaM/> [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|Collegiate national player of the year]], [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]],<ref name=GRIbtfsoaNptctMb/> [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|NBA first overall draft pick]], [[NBA Finals]] champion, and an eleven-year NBA veteran.
